Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‑01 - our rapidly developed humanoid platform being deployed in real industrial environments - and we’re growing the team to take it even further.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Software Engineer II to join our Platform Infrastructure team in San Diego. You’ll help build the software and tools that enable our robots to run trusted software on trusted hardware, working with security, firmware, and platform engineers across the device lifecycle.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and maintain software and tools for trusted boot and device provisioning, working with NVIDIA secure boot and UEFI. For example, you might help bring up a secure boot flow on a new device or build tooling to provision and verify device credentials.

 - Contribute to device trust and key protection using hardware roots of trust, including Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs), and security technologies such as ARM TrustZone.

 - Contribute to device key management though the use of Hardware Security Modules (HSMs).

 - Write, test, and debug software and scripts in Linux, and investigate issues across software and hardware.

 - Identify and reduce attack surfaces across device software, boot flows, and supporting tools.

 - Collaborate with security, firmware, cloud, manufacturing, and other engineering teams through design discussions, code reviews, and documentation; own well-scoped projects from design through implementation and testing, with input from experienced teammates.




WHAT YOU BRING

You’re a curious, collaborative engineer who takes ownership, works through unfamiliar problems, and wants to deepen your skills in device security. You’ll bring:

 - Software engineering experience — Typically 1–3 years of full-time experience building, testing, and maintaining production-quality software, or equivalent experience. 
   
   - You have a strong foundation in object-oriented programming and software design. 
   
   - You can read and reason about code, identify logic errors, and learn to contribute across C++, Python, and Rust codebases
   
   - Prior experience in all three languages is not required. B.S. or M.S. in CS, CE, EE, or a related field.

 - AI-assisted development — You’re comfortable using AI-assisted development tools and can understand, review, and validate the code they produce.

 - Security fundamentals — Familiarity with authentication, encryption, cryptographic keys, and trust boundaries, and an interest in applying them to hardware devices.

 - Linux and tooling — Comfort working in Linux and using scripting languages such as Python or Bash to automate tasks, build tools, and investigate problems.

 - Problem-solving and collaboration — A thoughtful approach to unfamiliar problems, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate clearly, seek feedback, and follow work through.

 - Experience with key management and/or NVIDIA platforms, such as Jetson, is a plus

 - Ability to work on-site at our San Diego office.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Comprehensive health coverage for US‑based employees, including fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance, with virtual care and employee assistance resources.

 - Meaningful time off to rest and recharge: 23 days of PTO (accrued), separate sick leave, and paid company holidays.

 - 401(k) retirement plan with employer match.

 - Equity included–we believe builders should share in what they build.

 - Free daily catered lunch, snacks, and drinks in‑office.

 - Collaboration with top‑tier engineers, researchers, and product experts in AI and robotics.

 - Freedom to influence the product and own key initiatives.
   
   

For this role in California, the expected base salary range is $123,000-$154,000 USD per year; your placement in that range depends on how your experience maps to our internal leveling.

Specializing in discretionary and quantitative macro strategies, Graham is dedicated to delivering strong, uncorrelated returns across a wide range of market environments. As one of the industry’s longest-standing global macro and trend-following managers, Graham remains committed to innovation, evolving its strategies through a robust investment, technology, and operational infrastructure. Graham harnesses the synergies between its discretionary and quantitative trading businesses to offer a broad suite of complementary alpha strategies, each built on the principles of thoughtful portfolio construction, active risk management, and diversification by design. Graham invests significant proprietary capital alongside its clients – including global institutions, endowments, foundations, family offices, sovereign wealth funds, investment management advisors, and qualified individual investors – reinforcing alignment of interests across all strategies.
The foundation of Graham’s sustainability and success is the experience and contributions of its people. The firm seeks to cultivate talent, encourage the diversity of ideas, and respect the contributions of all. In turn, each employee shares in the responsibility of strengthening those around them.
Description
Graham Capital Management, L.P. is seeking a junior-to-mid-level Software Developer to join its Trading Technology team in support of continued growth across its quantitative and discretionary trading businesses. The role will focus primarily on maintaining, enhancing, and supporting critical Windows client and server applications, while also contributing to new development projects. The successful candidate will work within a small, collaborative team and interact closely with development peers, the quantitative trading team, and other business users, with meaningful autonomy in developing technical solutions.
Responsibilities
Working closely with developers and business users, primarily within the quantitative trading team, to gather requirements and scope projects
Maintaining, enhancing, and updating existing Windows client and server applications, while also contributing to new development projects
Analyzing existing systems for robustness and performance improvements
Presenting ideas for system improvements, both technical and business-related
Producing product specifications and training peers and users on system use and maintenance
Performing unit, integration, and functional testing
Maintaining and supporting business-critical pre-trade signal and order generation systems through UAT and production, with a focus on accuracy, reliability, and timely processing
Requirements
Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field
1-5 years of relevant software development experience; strong recent graduates with relevant internship, academic, or project experience will also be considered. Prior financial services or investment management experience is not required
Strong object-oriented programming skills; C# is preferred, but strong candidates with experience in Java, Python, or another modern programming language will also be considered
Experience with or strong knowledge of concurrency, automated unit testing, and SQL
Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate with developers and business users throughout the software development life cycle
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to developing reliable, thoroughly tested software
Experience with event-driven architecture (messaging), F#, or functional programming (preferred)
This role requires commuting into our Rowayton, CT office Mondays through Fridays.
